_comment: Recommender gold set for the Part F harness (brief §11.2): 8 hand-labelled seeds. Four seeds (B3, B4, B5, C1) straddle the deliberately-adjacent B/C boundary, which is where the labelling judgement is actually tested. All four clusters are represented so the recommender is not graded only on topics the author tuned against. LABELLING POLICY — a document's own superseded lineage sibling is NOT labelled relevant: an analyst asking 'what else should I read after d516' is not helped by d516's own consultative draft, which says the same things in earlier wording. This is a judgement call with a measurable consequence, stated here so ablation 4 can be read honestly: because no gold list contains both members of a lineage pair, near-duplicate resolution can only help or be neutral on nDCG@5 in this set, and Duplicate Leakage has a true target of 0. Had the drafts been labelled relevant, dedup would have been penalised by nDCG while still being the right behaviour — the metric, not the method, would have been at fault.

cases._why: Foundational RAG paper. Useful next reads are the retriever it is built on, the survey that situates it, and the retrieval-structure advance that followed.
Broad survey (the §9.1 lambda-sweep seed). Straddles B/C: it covers the architecture papers and reaches into graph and evaluation territory.
RAPTOR builds a hierarchy of summaries over chunks; the genuinely useful follow-ups are the papers that also restructure the retrieval index, including the graph-community line. Straddles B/C.
Edge et al. is the bridge document — indexed in B, but its follow-ups are the graph-RAG cluster. Straddles B/C.
Graph-RAG survey; useful follow-ups are the graph systems it surveys plus the general RAG survey it complements. Straddles B/C.
RAGAS v1. C5 is its own v2 and is deliberately NOT labelled (see labelling policy). What remains genuinely useful are the surveys whose evaluation sections cover this ground.
d516 final. A2 is its own consultative draft and is deliberately NOT labelled. A3 is the companion PSMOR revision issued the same day; A5 is the FSI executive summary of these very principles.

Cluster D seed (untuned topic). Zero Trust Architecture's useful follow-ups are the maturity model that operationalises it, the framework it sits inside, and the identity guidance behind its first pillar.
